name: Ulster loyalism
summary: Ulster loyalism is the working-class Protestant strand of Ulster unionism. It holds that Northern Ireland must remain in the United Kingdom under the Crown, opposes Irish unification and Irish nationalism, and defends Protestant British culture, parades and flags. It has a paramilitary wing that justified violence in defence of the Union, and a political wing that shifted to political means after the 1994 ceasefires.
scope: Ulster loyalism as the scholarship on unionist ideology defines it: Todd's 'Ulster loyalism', a self-contained cultural community with a secondary political allegiance to the British state, set out by Cochrane (citing Todd, Miller, McGarry and O'Leary), with the loyalist politics Hall and Edwards and Bloomer describe. Excludes the Ulster British strand of unionism, and the platforms of paramilitary groups and parties (UDA, UVF, PUP), which are organisations, not the ideology.
